notes: Motive is our interpretation; Samsung did not state it.

claim: Inference: the 2025-26 memory upturn started with legacy DDR4 end-of-life (mid-2025) and AI server demand, accelerated in 4Q25 (conventional DRAM contract +45-50% QoQ) and peaked in 1Q26 (+93-98% QoQ) before slowing (3Q26 forecast +13-18%).
evidence: Sequence from TrendForce releases in this batch.

claim: Inference: memory contracting is shifting from quarterly (and in the 2025 shortage, monthly) price resets toward 3-5 year take-or-pay agreements with price bands and prepayments, a structural change from the pre-2026 model in which customers avoided long fixed-price contracts.
evidence: Combines @c_mureluct, @c_oldpractice, @c_monthly, @c_sca10q, @c_samlta, @c_ltaterms.
notes: Based on claims listed in evidence.

claim: Inference: states have repeatedly propped up memory makers in downturns: Korea via state-directed creditor support to Hynix (2001-03), Japan via DBJ equity in Elpida (2009), and China via Big Fund and local-government capital for YMTC and CXMT (2016-2026); only the Chinese entrants have grown, while Qimonda (no rescue agreed) and Elpida (rescued, then bankrupt) exited.
evidence: Reading of @c_cvd, @c_elpidaipa, @c_elpidadebt, @c_qim, @c_ymtc23, @c_cxmtstate, @c_cxmtbf.

claim: TrendForce reported that commodity DRAM contract prices fell 34% and spot prices 52% in 3Q08, while world DRAM revenue fell 2.4% QoQ to US$6.355 billion.
evidence: "Commodity DRAM contract price dropped 34% and spot price plunged to 52% in Q308."; "The WW Q3 DRAM revenue only slightly decreased 2.4% QoQ to 6.355 billion USD." (TrendForce, 10 Dec 2008)
